hook: Dario Amodei came to machine learning through physics and biology rather than computer science. He studied physics at Caltech and took a BS at Stanford, then a PhD at Princeton in computational neuroscience, where he built statistical models of real neural circuits in retina and cortex and performed the first recording of a complete half-millimetre patch of retina. His dissertation won the Hertz Doctoral Thesis Prize. Before that he had worked as a geophysicist at Schlumberger and as a consultant at Applied Minds, and afterwards spent three years as a Stanford postdoc writing proteomics software. He moved into deep learning at Baidu in 2014 under Andrew Ng, doing most of the machine learning research for Deep Speech 2, then Google Brain, then OpenAI, where he led the teams that built GPT-2 and GPT-3 and was one of two people setting overall research direction. He left in December 2020 and co-founded Anthropic two months later.

standing.standing: Dario Amodei is CEO and co-founder of Anthropic, a San Francisco startup founded in 2021. The records list him as an executive of Anthropic and as its founder. He previously led the teams that built GPT-2 and GPT-3 at OpenAI and was one of two people setting overall research direction. He left OpenAI in December 2020 and co-founded Anthropic two months later. quick_facts: CEO and co-founder of Anthropic since February 2021
Vice President of Research at OpenAI, having joined in 2016 as team lead for AI safety and risen through Research Director
Led the efforts to build GPT-2 and GPT-3, and was one of two people setting OpenAI's overall research direction
PhD in biophysics and computational neuroscience from Princeton; dissertation awarded the Hertz Doctoral Thesis Prize in 2012
BS in Physics from Stanford, after beginning at Caltech
Did the majority of the machine learning research for Baidu's Deep Speech 2, named by MIT Technology Review one of the top ten breakthrough technologies of 2016
Co-authored Concrete Problems in AI Safety at Google Brain with Chris Olah and others, one of the founding papers of the field
Worked as a geophysicist at Schlumberger and a consultant at Applied Minds before graduate school
Spent three years as a Stanford postdoctoral scholar building mass spectrometry and proteomics software, contributing 14,000 lines of code to the Skyline project

achievements.title: Anthropic
achievements.impact: Co-founded in February 2021 and leads as CEO, a public benefit corporation combining scaling with long-term alignment research to build steerable, interpretable and robust AI systems, and producing the Claude model family.

achievements.title: GPT-2 and GPT-3
achievements.impact: Led the efforts to build both at OpenAI. GPT-3 was among the largest language models trained to that point and established scaling as the central research direction of the field.

achievements.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
achievements.impact: Co-authored the 2016 paper laying out key problems in preventing accidents in AI systems, written at Google Brain with Chris Olah and others, and still one of the field's founding references.

achievements.title: Deep Speech 2
achievements.impact: Performed the majority of the machine learning research at Baidu, including architectures that cut relative word error rate by 35 percent in English and 15 percent in Chinese, and a tenfold decoder speedup that made deployment possible.

achievements.title: Computational neuroscience at Princeton
achievements.impact: Built Hopfield-style statistical models of biological neural networks, co-invented a device for in vivo intracellular recording, and performed the first recording of a complete 0.5 by 0.5 millimetre patch of retina.

achievements.title: Machines of Loving Grace
achievements.impact: His October 2024 essay arguing that AI's potential upside for medicine, neuroscience and economic development is widely underestimated, written by someone whose day job is arguing for caution.
